label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.4 a.2…: Every perfection of a thing whose being a cause…
locator: I q.4 a.2 co., first proof: quidquid perfectionis est in effectu, oportet inveniri in causa effectiva
interpretation: Whatever perfection is in the effect is in the effective cause, univocally or more eminently. 'Effect' is read as a thing whose being the cause causes, as in the application that immediately follows ('Cum ergo Deus sit prima causa effectiva rerum, oportet omnium rerum perfectiones praeexistere in Deo'). 'In the cause' is the same abstract InAct (formally or eminently) as in the prima via and q.11 a.3. The second proof (from ipsum esse subsistens) is not formalized; it is what would reach every perfection, not only those found in things.
